name: Kinsta
summary: Managed WordPress hosting on Google Cloud, with free migrations and 24/7 support. Overage bills per 1,000 extra visits; Kinsta gives no partner-only discount codes.
best_for: business-critical WordPress sites where speed, uptime and expert support directly affect revenue
skip_if: you run a small, low-traffic site on a tight budget — entry-level shared hosting or a caching plugin gets you most of the way for a fraction of the price
honest_knock: You're paying a premium for managed speed, Google Cloud infrastructure and expert support — worth it if performance and hands-off management matter, wasteful on a low-traffic hobby site a $5 shared host would carry fine.

pricing.entry_price_terms: a month, or $30 a month billed annually ($350/yr)
pricing.notes: (re-verified 2026-10-03 on their own plans page, USD, tax excluded) Managed WordPress hosting from $35/mo for a single site, or $30/mo billed annually at $350 a year, with the first month free on top — Kinsta advertises annual as two months off. That entry plan carries one WordPress install, 10GB storage, 20GB server bandwidth, 125GB CDN bandwidth and 14 days of backup retention, and you choose whether it is metered on bandwidth or on visits, which is a real change from the visit-only plans older reviews describe. The multi-site ladder runs WP 2 at $70/mo or $59 billed annually ($700 a year), WP 5 at $115 or $96 ($1,150), WP 10 at $225 or $188 ($2,250), WP 20 at $340 or $284 ($3,400) and WP 40 at $450 or $375 ($4,500). Agency plans start at that same $340/mo, or $284 billed annually. Above them sits an Enterprise line our earlier readings missed entirely: it starts at $500/mo, or $417 billed annually, with $5,000 payable on signup. Several things that look like plan features are priced separately — dedicated servers from $300/mo, PHP performance at $10 per 500MB a month, external backups to AWS or Google Cloud at $2 per site a month plus $1 per GB, and more frequent backups at $20 a site for six-hourly or $100 for hourly. It is a premium tier — cheaper shared hosts exist. There is no exclusive discount code to look for: Kinsta confirmed to us on 28 Jul 2026 that it gives no partner-only or affiliate-only discounts. Read on 3 October 2026 every figure above was unchanged, and the page also carries a visit-metered business ladder beside the install-counted one: Launch at $35/mo or $30 billed annually (1 install, 75,000 estimated visits, 15GB storage), Launch Plus $59 or $50 (1 install, 125,000), Build $69 or $58 (2 installs, 200,000), Expand $99 or $83 (5, 350,000), Scale $169 or $141 (10, 650,000) and Lead $299 or $250 (20 installs, 1,500,000 visits). Kinsta's overage documentation puts visit overage at $0.50 per 1,000 visits and bandwidth overage at $0.50 per GB.
